001: Manager Wang, does the client have any more feedback on the proposal?
They think the overall direction is fine, but the budget still needs further discussion.
So how much do you think we can afford to give in on our end?
I plan to hear their target price first, then decide how to negotiate.
Okay, just let me know once you've set up a time.
No problem, I'll contact them this afternoon.
002: Mr. Li, Manager Zhang just called and said he wants to see the samples earlier.
That's fine. Arrange it and have them delivered to their company tomorrow morning.
Okay, should I also prepare a detailed presentation document?
Yes, it's best to organize the technical specs and the price quote as well.
Understood, I'll get on it right away.
Thanks for your hard work. Keep me updated on any developments.
003: Mr. Chen, regarding the delivery date in the contract, we'd like to confirm it once more.
Our original plan was mid-next month, but raw materials have been a bit tight lately.
So how long do you estimate the delay might be?
If things go smoothly, it might only be about a week late.
Okay, then we'll adjust our production schedule based on that.
I'm really sorry, and I hope you can understand our situation.
004: Mr. Liu, a client complained that two boxes from our last shipment arrived damaged.
Really? Then check right away whether it's a shipping issue or a packaging issue.
I looked at the photos, and it seems to be from jostling during transit.
Alright, first send the client two replacement boxes, and we'll cover the shipping cost.
Okay, I'll contact the logistics company right away to handle it.
From now on, remind them to reinforce the packaging before shipping. We can't let this happen again.
005: Mr. Zhao, are you satisfied with our newly proposed design plan?
The overall feel is good, but I think the color scheme is a bit too dark.
So would you prefer a brighter style?
Yes, it'd be best if it were a bit more lively, to match our brand's positioning.
Understood, I'll have the designer adjust the color palette.
Great, thanks for your hard work. Once it's revised, we'll set up another time to review it.
006: Mr. Sun, the client's company wants to send two people to tour our factory.
Sure, that works. Arrange a specific time and itinerary.
They want to see the production line and the quality inspection process. It'll probably take about half a day.
Fine, let's set it for next Wednesday morning. Prepare the reception in advance.
Okay, I'll get the materials and the tour route ready.
Make sure to take some photos then, to keep for future promotional use.
007: Manager Zhou, the client raised an objection to our quote, saying it's too high.
Which part specifically do they think is too expensive?
Mainly the labor costs. They say it's quite a bit higher than the market rate.
Then explain to them that we only use experienced workers.
I already explained that, but they still hope we can lower it a bit.
Tell you what, if the order volume is large enough, we can offer a discount.
008: Mr. Wu, the client just called and said they want to place an additional order.
That's great news. How much more do they want?
About thirty percent more than the original order.
Will we make the deadline? Is our current production capacity enough?
I did the math, and if we work overtime, it should be fine.
Good, then coordinate with the production department and do your best to meet the client's needs.
009: Mr. Zheng, regarding the payment terms you mentioned last time, we discussed it internally.
So what's the verdict? Can you accept installment payments?
Yes, but we'd like the down payment ratio to be raised to fifty percent.
That ratio is a bit high. We can't come up with that much cash all at once.
Then how about forty percent? That's our bottom line.
Alright, I'll go back and discuss it with our finance team, and get back to you as soon as possible.
010: Mr. He, the client has made a new request regarding our after-sales service.
What request? Tell me about it.
They want us to extend the warranty period to two years.
Two years is a bit long. Our standard is one year, and the most we can extend it to is a year and a half.
Then I'll go talk to them and see if they can accept that.
Okay, try your best to convince them. If that really doesn't work, we'll think of another way.
